goal: Port lexical.stutter to v3 natively: Corpus altitude, walks the scope tree owner chain (the v3 scope hierarchy replaces the legacy manual AST scope-stack walk). For each callable/class, if its name tokens repeat an enclosing scope's name tokens (>= min_overlap_tokens, noise-excluded), emit a directed DROP_REDUNDANT_TOKENS WARNING verdict at the deepest stutter — the scope already provides the repeated token. Legacy stutter.py as oracle for the signal (not the implementation).

summary.title: Port lexical.stutter (scope-restatement verdict)
summary.what: Corpus-altitude lexical.stutter reading the enclosing-scope hierarchy off the scope-tree owner chain. A name whose tokens repeat an enclosing class/module/package name -> directed DROP_REDUNDANT_TOKENS WARNING verdict at the deepest stutter. Registry 24; 4 tests.
summary.why: Completes the lexical family. The v3 scope tree supplies the enclosing-scope stack natively, so the legacy manual AST scope-stack walk is unnecessary; the fix is mechanical so a directed verdict.

decisions.chose: Walk the scope-tree owner chain, not the AST
decisions.rationale: The v3 scope hierarchy already encodes enclosing scopes; reading overlap off owners is simpler and exact (legacy=oracle for the signal, not the implementation).
rejected: Re-walk the AST with a manual scope stack (the legacy 520-LOC approach)
